title: [observation] check:type-check-coverage's test-layer count is `exclude`-shaped, so a package that simply omits `test/` from `include` is invisible to it
body:
Filed unassigned by the #7312 dev (PR for #7312) as an out-of-scope observation. Not fixed there: #7312's surface is the two example apps' tsconfigs, and changing what this gate counts changes the ratchet for every package in the repo.

## The shape

`scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` decides whether a package hides its tests from tsc by reading the tsconfig's **`exclude`** array only:

```js
excludesTests: (parsed.exclude ?? []).some((pattern) => TEST_GLOB.test(pattern)),
```

`roots` is computed from `include` a few lines above and is used by `configCovers` for the PINS_CHECKED walk — but it never feeds `excludesTests`. So the gate detects "this config steers tsc **away** from the tests" and does not detect "this config never steered tsc **toward** them".

A package whose tsconfig has no `exclude` at all, and whose `include` is `["src/**/*"]` with a sibling `test/` tree, therefore reports as fully test-covered.

## Measured

`examples/app-crm` and `examples/app-todo` were exactly that shape (no `exclude`; `include` omitted `test/**/*`) — the subject of #7312. Running the gate before and after the #7312 fix, which moved both apps from hiding their tests to compiling them:

```
before: test layer: 19 package(s) still exclude their own tests (646 files hidden ...)
after:  test layer: 19 package(s) still exclude their own tests (646 files hidden ...)
```

Identical. Two apps' worth of test files entered a tsc program and the gate's count did not move, because neither app ever counted toward it.

Corroborating measurement from the same run: with the pre-#7312 tsconfigs in place, a deliberate `TS2322` planted in `app-crm/test/opportunity-stage-hook.test.ts` and another in `app-todo/test/task-recurrence.test.ts` left both apps' `tsc --noEmit` green **and** left this gate reporting OK.

## Scope of the blind spot

The script's own comment on `countRoots` is aware of the adjacent case and routes it elsewhere:

> Several packages keep a sibling `test/` tree that their `include` never mentions -- counting it here would attribute files to an exclusion that has no bearing on them (PINS_CHECKED is what covers those).

That hand-off is only partial: PINS_CHECKED collects test files carrying a `@ts-expect-error` directive. A test tree outside `include` whose files carry no pin directive is reported by neither half.

Not measured here: how many packages repo-wide are in the `include`-shaped form versus the `exclude`-shaped one. That count is the first thing a fix would need, since it sets how far the ratchet moves on the day the gate starts seeing them.

## Why observation-class rather than a defect

Nothing a user hits, and the gate is not wrong about anything it does report — the ledger numbers it prints are real. The cost is that its headline ("N packages still exclude their own tests") reads as a complete inventory of the test-layer gap and is not one, so a package can drift into the uncounted shape without the ratchet noticing.
